job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: Plants exhibit diverse methods of reproduction to ensure their survival. While many people assume plants only grow from seeds, vegetative propagation allows plants like potatoes to grow from stem tubers. In sexual reproduction, flowers serve as the reproductive organs. A typical flower contains both male and female parts, but some species possess only one type. Pollination is the process where pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma, which is distinct from fertilisation, the actual fusion of male and female gametes occurring deep inside the ovary. Insects visit flowers to collect nectar for food, not to intentionally assist in plant reproduction. Furthermore, botanically speaking, fruits are the ripened ovaries of a flower; thus, tomatoes and cucumbers are classified as fruits because they contain seeds, regardless of their culinary use as vegetables. Finally, some simple organisms like Spirogyra reproduce through fragmentation, where the body breaks into two or more pieces, each growing into a new individual. Unlike seeds, which are complex structures, spores are single-celled units produced by ferns and mosses that do not require two parents to form a new plant. These various strategies demonstrate that nature is not limited to a single way of creating new life.

items.evidence: While many people assume plants only grow from seeds, vegetative propagation allows plants like potatoes to grow from stem tubers.
items.q: Meena plants a piece of potato that has no seeds. What will most likely happen?
options: A new plant grows from the potato piece
Nothing grows, since every plant needs seeds
The potato piece rots, since cut pieces die
A plant grows only if pollen lands on it
items.explain: Potatoes reproduce by vegetative propagation: a new plant grows from the stem tuber, without seeds.

wrong.why: thinks plants can only grow from seeds
thinks a cut living thing always dies
thinks pollen is the seed of the plant

items.evidence: Pollination is the process where pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma, which is distinct from fertilisation, the actual fusion of male and female gametes occurring deep inside the ovary.
items.q: Pollen has just landed on a flower's stigma. Has fertilisation happened yet?
options: No, the gametes fuse later inside the ovary
Yes, landing on the stigma is fertilisation
Yes, the gametes fuse on the stigma surface
No, fertilisation happens inside the anther
items.explain: Pollen reaching the stigma is pollination; fertilisation is the fusion of gametes deep inside the ovary.

wrong.why: thinks pollination and fertilisation are the same
thinks fertilisation happens on the stigma
picks another flower part named in the sentence

items.evidence: Insects visit flowers to collect nectar for food, not to intentionally assist in plant reproduction.
items.q: Why do bees keep visiting flowers in a garden?
options: To feed on the sweet nectar inside
To help the plant make its seeds
To carry the flower's seeds far away
To fertilise the flower on its stigma
items.explain: Insects visit flowers to collect nectar for food, not to help the plant reproduce on purpose.

wrong.why: thinks insects want to help plants reproduce
thinks pollen carried by bees is seed
thinks fertilisation happens on the stigma

items.evidence: Furthermore, botanically speaking, fruits are the ripened ovaries of a flower; thus, tomatoes and cucumbers are classified as fruits because they contain seeds, regardless of their culinary use as vegetables.
items.q: Ravi cuts a tomato and finds seeds inside. What would a botanist call it?
options: A fruit, since it is a ripened ovary
A vegetable, since it is cooked in curry
A seed pod, since pollen grew into seeds
A tuber, since it grows like a potato
items.explain: Botanically, a tomato is a ripened ovary with seeds, so it is a fruit, whatever its kitchen use.

wrong.why: thinks tomatoes are vegetables because of cooking
thinks pollen is the seed of the flower
mixes it up with the potato example nearby

items.evidence: Unlike seeds, which are complex structures, spores are single-celled units produced by ferns and mosses that do not require two parents to form a new plant.
items.q: How is a fern spore different from a seed?
options: It is one cell and needs one parent
It is a tiny seed with the same parts
It forms only after insects pollinate ferns
It needs pollen from two parents to grow
items.explain: Seeds are complex, but spores are single cells that need no second parent to form a plant.

wrong.why: thinks spores are just very tiny seeds
thinks all plants rely on insects to reproduce
thinks pollen is needed like a seed
